top_signal.title: Struggling to transition my agency from SMM to Digital Infrastructure. Need some advice.
top_signal.summary: I'm building Machfold Ventures, a solo venture based in Mumbai.   Initially, I focused on social media marketing, content creation and digital marketing. However, I'm trying to move away from the conventional SMM agency model and focus more on digital infrastructure for SMEs.   Like websites, workflow automation, digital presence and operational solutions.   The problem? I'm finding it difficult to sell this to traditional Indian businesses.   Most business owners I approach just want someone to manage their Instagram, make reels and post content.   Recently, I even had a prospect whom I'd followed up with for a week. When I explained our shift towards digital infrastructure, he basically said, "I just need social media. Will you do that?" After a few postponed meetings, he ghosted me.   I'm now questioning my approach.   A few things I'd like advice on:   SMM: Should I retain it as an entry-level service and gradually upsell infrastructure solutions, or move away from it entirely?   Sales: For Mumbai SMEs, are cold calls or physical walk-ins more effective?   Positioning: How do you sell services like automation, websites and business systems to owners who don't necessarily realise they need them?   Niche: Should I focus on one industry (restaurants, clinics, retailers, etc.) instead of approaching every kind of business?   Would appreciate advice from anyone who's actually sold B2B services or worked with traditional Indian SMEs.   Trying to figure out how to make
